firstTimeAclModel.populationRule: No ACL rupture or ACL reconstruction before the prediction index.
firstTimeAclModel.outcome: Future medically confirmed noncontact or indirect-contact first ACL rupture within the pre-specified horizon.
firstTimeAclModel.rationale: First-time ACL studies evaluate pre-injury intrinsic, neuromuscular, biomechanical, strength, and exposure factors in previously ACL-uninjured athletes.

evidence.note: Adolescent female elite football/handball athletes without previous ACL injury; candidate factors included hip flexion at initial contact, internal knee rotation, semitendinosus preactivation, and external hip rotator strength.

Parental ACL history, body weight, anterior tibial displacement, genu recurvatum, and generalized joint laxity were associated with first-time noncontact ACL injury in both sexes; additional factors differed by sex.

Elite female footballers; reported associations included prior ACL history, dynamic knee valgus, ipsilateral trunk flexion, CMJ peak take-off force, and hip adductor:abductor strength ratio. Use as literature context, not universal coefficients.

secondaryAclModel.populationRule: Documented ACL rupture or reconstruction before the prediction index.
secondaryAclModel.outcome: Future medically confirmed ipsilateral graft or contralateral noncontact/indirect-contact ACL injury within the pre-specified horizon, with side recorded.
secondaryAclModel.rationale: Post-ACL-reconstruction biomechanics, rehabilitation, graft status, time since surgery, return-to-sport exposure, and contralateral risk make this a different prediction problem.

evidence.note: In 756 elite female handball/soccer players, knee biomechanics differed after ACL injury, but the seven knee-specific cutting variables were not associated with future secondary ACL injury in the previously injured group.

performanceRealityCheck.note: An extensive 3D motion-analysis and physical screening battery in 791 elite female handball/soccer players with 60 ACL injuries achieved mean AUROC 0.63 for the best classifier, with substantial repetition variability. Webcam ML should not be assumed to outperform this without evidence.

kamSurrogateBoundary.note: Clinic measures can predict high knee-abduction-moment status, but a KAM-surrogate equation is not itself an ACL-tear probability equation. The later prospective ACL analysis did not establish pKAM as a direct ACL injury predictor.
